_comment: Per-format baseline for the CI throughput gate (benchmarks/throughput.py). NOT a
dev-box measurement: record it from format-benchmarks-* CI artifacts with
The gate reads each format relative to the other formats in the same run, so only
the RATIOS between these numbers matter, not their absolute scale. That is what
makes a CPU-class change (0.57x / 0.73x / 1.0x in the #183 study) invisible to it.
The tolerance is set against the #183 replay of 1,003 CI runs: relative-to-run
spread is a robust sigma of 1.5-4% per format, CPU classes shift it by at most 9%,
and single-run contention bursts reach 3.4x on one format - which is why the gate
needs the slowdown in both passes. 30% caught an injected 1.5x slowdown 99% of
the time and 2x every time, with no false SLOW over the replay.
Re-record in the commit that changes a format's cost on purpose. Do not re-record
to chase a red run whose slowdown you did not intend.

provenance.source: format-benchmarks-* artifacts of every main-branch CI run 2026-09-16..2026-10-12
provenance.statistic: min over iterations; each run rescaled by its median ratio before the per-format median
